runtime.execution: Python ASGI service invocation runs through a protocol VM; async run actions or sync actions in a thread executor. Server owns durable storage/replay/scheduling.
runtime.service_boundary: Consumes Restate server and user external systems; SDK owns only invocation attempt/client resources, not an agent loop or shared service governor.

summary: Python context APIs for journaled code, state, calls, waits and invocation identity

inspection.scope: context contracts and server_context run/replay/proposal/state/RPC/teardown; direct retry and disconnect tests
inspection.limits: Core protocol VM and server durability studied separately; SDK source alone does not certify settlement of arbitrary external effects.

actions.name: ctx.run / ctx.run_typed(name, action, options, *args)
actions.input: Sync/async function, args/serde and retry overrides
actions.output: Serialized result or terminal failure via VM durable handle
actions.lifecycle: Recorded result replay bypasses closure; external effect precedes result proposal and may repeat if not durably settled
actions.authority: Developer/client programs execute arbitrary action; host credentials/OS authority

actions.name: ctx.get/set/state_keys/clear/clear_all
actions.lifecycle: Server VM state/journal; no persistent Python locals across attempts

actions.name: ctx.service_call/object_call/workflow_call and *_send
actions.input: Handler, serialized arg, object/workflow key, idempotency/scope/limit and optional delay
actions.output: Durable call future or send handle/invocation identity
actions.lifecycle: Server schedules/correlates calls; delayed/background send independent of local await

actions.name: ctx.awakeable/promise/signal; resolve/reject
actions.input: Opaque awakeable ID or invocation ID/name and payload
actions.lifecycle: Server retains pending wait; does not keep Python process stack alive
actions.authority: Client/external signal sender with endpoint authority

actions.name: ctx.cancel_invocation / attach_invocation
actions.output: Cancellation command or future attached to result
actions.lifecycle: Protocol cancel does not prove arbitrary external thread/side effect stopped
actions.authority: Context invoker; server controls durable invocation

actions.name: ctx.time/random/uuid; request.attempt_finished_event
actions.output: Journaled wall timestamp, deterministic RNG/UUID, local cleanup signal
actions.lifecycle: Stable per invocation replay; attempt signal closes/cancels client resources, no universal quiescence

evidence.claim: Run schedules action only when VM does not replay result; returns durable future handle.
Async action or executor-thread action runs before success/failure proposal; serialized result, wall-clock attempt duration and retry overrides.
VM state reads/writes, encoded values and request/attempt/idempotency identity.
Handler/serde discovery and delayed send with key/idempotency/scope/limit, underlying protocol VM dispatch.
Awakeable ID+future, promise, cancel and attach invocation primitives.
Attempt task list cancels futures, clears list; no wait for underlying executor thread.
Teardown flushes protocol output, waits input close, closes output; finished event then cancels tasks.
Addressed signal and stable seeded UUID/random; time implemented as journaled wall-time action.
Attempt-finished resource-cleanup contract, not guarantee arbitrary third-party call physically ended.
Server integration retry-after/terminal-error test counts exactly two attempts; latest container image not pinned by test helper.
Fake receive channel checks finite prompt disconnect result after drained queue; concrete no-hang oracle.

tests.oracle: Real server service test literal attempts==2; helper uses latest image, not pinned server. No action-success-before-journal crash oracle here.
Fake ASGI stream returns known event sequence; wait_for and literal disconnect checks bound liveness fault. Not run.

strengths: Explicit journal result versus local action execution and invocation/attempt identity.
Protocol disconnect/retry tests attack actual lifecycle faults.
limits: Durability is external server composition; arbitrary side effects can occur before result settlement.
Attempt-finished or canceled executor future is not physical external quiescence.
arconaut_questions: Which external actions require idempotency/reconciliation before a durable result can safely support replay?
Can refit account for executor threads and external calls rather than treating attempt-finished as enough?
